detections.description: A service, task, autorun, cron job or unit refers to a path that a filesystem finding (world-writable, temporary, unsigned, hidden or recently modified executable) also lists.

explanation.confidence_rationale: Confidence medium: Linking is by a shared path string in two independent findings; the path is exact but the file's purpose is still unknown.
explanation.disclaimer: These independent indicators were correlated by a rule. Correlation raises a question; it does not prove malicious activity.
missing_corroboration: Hash and signature of the file; creation time relative to the startup entry.
Network connections made by the process started from this path.
possible_benign_causes: Software legitimately installed under ProgramData or /opt that is also unsigned or recently updated.
explanation.severity_rationale: Severity high is the rule's base severity: A startup mechanism that points at a file sitting in an unsafe place or flagged as unusual is the shape of a planted foothold. The number of matching items did not change it.
explanation.why_correlated: Rule DR-ANY-COR-001 requires: (start all file). Satisfied clauses: start (1 item(s)), file (1 item(s)). The contributing items were grouped because they share evidence.paths = 'c:\\users\\public\\payload.exe'.
explanation.why_flagged: Two independent collectors (startup configuration and file inspection) describe the same path. That agreement is stronger than either finding alone and shows where to look first.

investigation_steps: Open the shared path: owner, hash, signature, timestamps.
Read the startup entry that references it.
Check whether other entries reference the same path.

matched_conditions.description: A suspicious service, task, autorun or cron/unit finding
A filesystem finding about an unusual executable or writable file

attack.explanation: Service/unit persistence can launch attacker-placed files; here the link is only a shared path.
Scheduled execution can launch attacker-placed files; here the link is only a shared path.

detections.remediation: Preserve the file and the entry as evidence, disable the startup entry, then remove or restore the file from a trusted source.

rule.name: Persistence entry executes a file that the filesystem checks also flagged

detections.title: Persistence entry runs a file flagged by the filesystem checks: C:\Users\Public\payload.exe

detections.description: A log-impairment or protection-disabling finding appears on the same host as a high-signal persistence finding.

explanation.confidence_rationale: Confidence medium: Both are accurate findings; their link is that they co-occur, not that one caused the other.
explanation.disclaimer: These independent indicators were correlated by a rule. Correlation raises a question; it does not prove malicious activity.
missing_corroboration: Timestamps showing the persistence artefact was created after logging was reduced.
possible_benign_causes: Hosts with custom logging pipelines that look impaired to the collector, plus an unrelated admin script flagged as persistence.
explanation.severity_rationale: Severity high is the rule's base severity: Persistence indicators are concerning on their own; paired with reduced logging or protection they suggest the host was prepared to avoid detection. The number of matching items did not change it.
explanation.why_correlated: Rule DR-ANY-COR-005 requires: (impair all persist). Satisfied clauses: impair (2 item(s)), persist (1 item(s)).
explanation.why_flagged: Attackers who establish persistence commonly also reduce what is recorded. Co-occurrence prioritises this host for investigation over hosts with only one of the signals.

investigation_steps: Establish the timeline from file and configuration timestamps.
Check whether other hosts show the same pair.
Collect volatile evidence (processes, connections) before changing anything.

attack.explanation: Impairing defences is a tactic used alongside persistence; co-occurrence here does not prove it.

detections.remediation: Restore logging and protection, preserve and then remove the persistence artefact, and review the host for further changes.

rule.name: Logging or protection impaired alongside a persistence indicator

detections.title: Reduced logging/protection together with a persistence indicator

detections.description: The host firewall is disabled, default-allow, or allows everything inbound, and remote-management or database ports are listening on non-loopback addresses.

explanation.confidence_rationale: Confidence medium: Both facts are exact; a network firewall in front of the host may still provide protection that is not visible here.
explanation.disclaimer: These independent indicators were correlated by a rule. Correlation raises a question; it does not prove malicious activity.
missing_corroboration: Confirmation from network scans or upstream ACLs that the ports are reachable.
Firewall configuration changes since the previous snapshot.
possible_benign_causes: Hosts protected by a dedicated upstream firewall and reachable only from a management VLAN.
explanation.severity_rationale: Severity high is the rule's base severity: With no effective host filtering, every listed service is reachable by anything that can route to the host. The number of matching items did not change it.
explanation.why_correlated: Rule DR-ANY-NET-002 requires: (fw all svc). Satisfied clauses: fw (1 item(s)), svc (2 item(s)).
explanation.why_flagged: A host firewall is the last filter for services bound to every interface. Its absence plus a listening management or database port is a concrete exposure, not just a hygiene gap.

investigation_steps: Verify reachability of the listed ports from an untrusted segment.
Check upstream filtering and the firewall change history.
Identify owners of the listening services.

matched_conditions.description: Host firewall disabled, default-allow or allow-all
A management or data port listening on a non-loopback address

attack.explanation: Exposed services without filtering enlarge the attack surface for exploitation of public-facing applications; none is exploited here.

detections.remediation: Enable the host firewall with an allow-list for required ports (reload rather than flush; verify scored ports first), or bind the services to loopback.

rule.name: Host firewall absent or permissive while management or data services listen

detections.title: Open host firewall with listening management/data services

detections.description: An unexpected or over-privileged account configuration was found on a host that also has weak authentication controls.

explanation.confidence_rationale: Confidence medium: Both sides are exact findings; their relationship (same accounts, reachable service) is not established by the data.
explanation.disclaimer: These independent indicators were correlated by a rule. Correlation raises a question; it does not prove malicious activity.
missing_corroboration: Evidence that the weak control applies to the privileged account (for example sshd allowing that account).
Logons by the privileged account from unusual sources.
possible_benign_causes: Competition or lab hosts configured deliberately weak.
explanation.severity_rationale: Severity high was set by an explicit rule condition: An authentication-bypass-class weakness (PAM accepts without credential, passwordless accounts, no NLA, auto-logon) is present.
explanation.why_correlated: Rule DR-ANY-PRIV-002 requires: (priv all auth). Satisfied clauses: priv (1 item(s)), auth (1 item(s)), bypass (1 item(s)).
explanation.why_flagged: An attacker needs a way to authenticate and a privileged identity to use. Seeing a questionable privileged account and weak authentication on one host is more actionable than either alone.

investigation_steps: Check whether the privileged account can use the weak authentication path (sshd AllowUsers, PAM stack for the service).
Review authentication logs for the privileged accounts.
Fix the bypass-class weakness first.

attack.explanation: Valid accounts are often used with weak authentication to gain access; nothing here shows use.
Account manipulation is one way a privileged anomaly arises.

detections.remediation: Remove or justify the anomalous privileged account, then close the authentication weakness (PAM/sshd/NLA/lockout) in the order of the severity rationale.

rule.name: Privileged-account anomaly together with weak authentication settings

detections.title: Privileged-account anomaly with weak authentication on host01

detections.description: An enabled local account has a name ending in $ (hidden from some tools) or does not require a password.

explanation.confidence_rationale: Confidence medium: Machine-style names and passwordless service accounts exist legitimately in some environments.
explanation.disclaimer: This is a suspicious indicator. Benign activity can produce the same observation; it does not prove compromise.
missing_corroboration: Optional corroboration not observed: An enabled account without a required password
possible_benign_causes: Legacy service accounts created without passwords for local-only use.
explanation.severity_rationale: Severity high is the rule's base severity: Either condition gives access without a normal visible, authenticated account. The number of matching items did not change it.
explanation.why_correlated: Rule DR-WIN-ACC-001 requires: (nopass any hidden). Satisfied clauses: hidden (1 item(s)). The contributing items were grouped because they share key = 'user:S-1-5-21-1-1003'.
explanation.why_flagged: A $-suffixed name hides an account from net user and some GUIs; a password-not-required flag lets the account authenticate with a blank password if policy allows.

investigation_steps: Compare the account against the documented account list and its creation time.
Check group memberships (especially Administrators) and recent logons.
Review the registry SAM entry creation time if available.

matched_conditions.description: An enabled local account whose name ends in $

attack.explanation: Hidden or passwordless local accounts are a way to keep access; creation by an adversary is not shown.
A $-suffixed account name hides the account from some listings (Hidden Users technique family).

detections.remediation: Disable or remove unauthorised accounts after preserving evidence; require passwords on all enabled accounts.

rule.name: Enabled local account that is hidden or needs no password

detections.title: Suspicious local account configuration: (none)support$

detections.description: LSA/credential-protection settings are weak and UAC or Microsoft Defender is also weakened.

explanation.confidence_rationale: Confidence medium: The settings are exact; whether they were weakened deliberately is not known.
explanation.disclaimer: These independent indicators were correlated by a rule. Correlation raises a question; it does not prove malicious activity.
missing_corroboration: Event log evidence of LSASS access or of Defender tamper events.
Changes to these settings since the previous snapshot.
possible_benign_causes: Legacy compatibility settings kept for old applications (for example WDigest for old SSO).
explanation.severity_rationale: Severity high was set by an explicit rule condition: Microsoft Defender protection is disabled, removing the main control against credential-dumping tools.
explanation.why_correlated: Rule DR-WIN-CRED-001 requires: (lsa all posture). Satisfied clauses: lsa (1 item(s)), posture (1 item(s)), defender (1 item(s)).
explanation.why_flagged: Credential-dumping tools need weak LSA protection and little interference from endpoint protection. Seeing both together is a preparation pattern, though it also matches poorly hardened hosts.

investigation_steps: Check when each setting was changed (registry key last-write times, GPO history).
Review Defender operational logs for disabled or excluded paths.
Look for tools in user-writable folders (see the filesystem findings).

matched_conditions.description: A weak LSA or credential-protection setting
UAC weakened or Defender disabled / broadly excluded

attack.explanation: Weak LSA protection facilitates LSASS credential dumping; no dumping is observed.
Disabled or excluded endpoint protection can indicate impairment of defences; it can also be misconfiguration.

detections.remediation: Enable RunAsPPL, disable WDigest, restore UAC and Defender defaults, and remove broad exclusions; test for application compatibility first.

rule.name: Credential protections weakened alongside weakened endpoint defences

detections.title: Credential protections and endpoint defences are both weakened

detections.description: A persistence mechanism that normal software rarely uses (WMI event consumers, IFEO debuggers, AppInit/AppCert DLLs, LSA packages, Winlogon changes, accessibility-binary replacement, ...) is configured.

explanation.confidence_rationale: Confidence medium: Security and accessibility products occasionally use these hooks; the collector already filters stock Windows values.
explanation.disclaimer: This is a suspicious indicator. Benign activity can produce the same observation; it does not prove compromise.
missing_corroboration: Binary signature, hash reputation and creation time of the referenced file or consumer.
The same artefact appearing in an earlier snapshot (then it is long-standing, not new).
possible_benign_causes: Endpoint security and application-compatibility tools that register WMI consumers, IFEO entries or AppInit DLLs.
explanation.severity_rationale: Severity high is the rule's base severity: These locations are rarely configured by legitimate software and execute code automatically. The number of matching items did not change it.
explanation.why_correlated: Rule DR-WIN-PER-001 requires: per. Satisfied clauses: per (1 item(s)). Each matching item is reported separately (grouped by id = 'BOF-acf909c8fdaf4d4b').
explanation.why_flagged: Run keys are common and noisy; these mechanisms are specifically chosen by adversaries to execute code at logon, boot or process start without appearing in the usual autorun lists.

investigation_steps: Open the evidence reference and read the configured command or DLL.
Verify the signature and compare the hash with a trusted source.
Establish when it was added (registry last-write, WMI repository, event logs) and by which account.

attack.explanation: WMI event subscription persistence is one of the checks covered (PER-WMI-001).
Image File Execution Options injection is covered by PER-IFEO-001.
Winlogon helper changes are covered by AUT-WINLOGON-001.

detections.remediation: Capture the artefact, then remove or disable the mechanism and the binary it points to; reset the registry value to its Windows default.

rule.name: Registry or WMI persistence mechanism commonly used for stealthy execution

detections.title: Stealthy persistence mechanism configured: Synthetic finding PER-WMI-001

detections.description: A service that runs as LocalSystem (or another built-in privileged account) has its executable under Users, ProgramData or Temp.

explanation.confidence_rationale: Confidence medium: Some software legitimately installs services under ProgramData, and the data does not show the folder's permissions.
explanation.disclaimer: This is a suspicious indicator. Benign activity can produce the same observation; it does not prove compromise.
missing_corroboration: ACLs on the binary and its directory showing write access for non-administrators.
Missing or invalid Authenticode signature on the binary.
possible_benign_causes: Per-machine installers that place agent services under ProgramData.
explanation.severity_rationale: Severity high is the rule's base severity: Anyone who can write the binary or its folder gains SYSTEM privileges when the service starts. The number of matching items did not change it.
explanation.why_correlated: Rule DR-WIN-SVC-001 requires: svc. Satisfied clauses: svc (1 item(s)). Each matching item is reported separately (grouped by key = 'service:evilsvc').
explanation.why_flagged: A SYSTEM service whose binary lives where standard users can write is a ready-made privilege escalation and a common persistence location.

investigation_steps: Check the signature and hash of the binary and its folder ACLs.
Find out when the service was created (event 7045) and by whom.
Look for sibling services or tasks pointing at the same folder.

matched_conditions.description: A privileged service with an image path in a user-writable folder

attack.explanation: Services are a common Windows persistence mechanism; this shows exposure, not creation by an adversary.

detections.remediation: Move the binary to a protected location or reinstall the product; remove the service if unauthorised (disable first).

rule.name: Privileged service runs a binary from a user-writable path

detections.title: Privileged service runs from a user-writable path: service:evilsvc

detections.description: A scheduled task running as SYSTEM or with the highest run level executes a file in a user-writable folder.

explanation.confidence_rationale: Confidence medium: Update agents sometimes keep helpers in ProgramData; folder permissions are not part of the data.
explanation.disclaimer: This is a suspicious indicator. Benign activity can produce the same observation; it does not prove compromise.
possible_benign_causes: Vendor update tasks that stage executables under ProgramData.
explanation.severity_rationale: Severity high is the rule's base severity: A task that runs with SYSTEM rights from a folder users can write to is both an escalation path and a persistence mechanism. The number of matching items did not change it.
explanation.why_correlated: Rule DR-WIN-TSK-001 requires: task. Satisfied clauses: task (1 item(s)). Each matching item is reported separately (grouped by key = 'task:\\updater\\sync').
explanation.why_flagged: Scheduled tasks start at boot or logon with the task's privileges; pointing one at a writable folder is a standard Windows persistence pattern.

investigation_steps: Export the task XML and check its author, creation date and triggers.
Verify the executable's signature and hash.
Check for other tasks created at the same time.

matched_conditions.description: A privileged task with an action in a user-writable folder

attack.explanation: Scheduled tasks are a documented persistence and escalation mechanism; the data does not show who created this one.

detections.remediation: Disable the task if unauthorised (disable, then remove after evidence capture) and restrict write access to the folder.

rule.name: Privileged scheduled task runs from a user-writable path

detections.title: Privileged scheduled task runs from a user-writable path: task:\updater\sync

detections.description: Three or more different logging weaknesses (Event Log service, disabled channels, audit policy, PowerShell logging, log size) are present.

explanation.confidence_rationale: Confidence medium: The findings are accurate individually; whether they were set deliberately is unknown.
explanation.disclaimer: These independent indicators were correlated by a rule. Correlation raises a question; it does not prove malicious activity.
missing_corroboration: Event log service stop/start events (7036) or log-clear events (1102, 104) in the retained logs.
Evidence that these settings were configured after the baseline.
possible_benign_causes: Freshly installed or unmanaged hosts that never had logging policy applied.
explanation.severity_rationale: Severity medium is the rule's base severity: Each weakness reduces visibility; together they leave little to investigate with, but they also describe an unconfigured host as readily as a tampered one. The number of matching items did not change it.
explanation.why_correlated: Rule DR-WIN-LOG-001 requires: weak. Satisfied clauses: weak (3 item(s)).
explanation.why_flagged: Adversaries reduce logging before acting. Several independent gaps in one area are worth checking together, but the severity stays medium because default Windows installs also show several of them.

investigation_steps: Compare each setting with the organisation's logging baseline and group policy.
Look for log clear events and Event Log service state changes.
Check whether settings changed since the previous assessment.

matched_conditions.description: Logging or audit-configuration findings (at least 3 different checks)

attack.explanation: Disabling or reducing Windows event logging is an evasion technique; these findings may equally reflect default settings.

detections.remediation: Apply the organisation's audit policy, enable PowerShell script block logging, set adequate log sizes and forward events off the host.
